newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended slightly lower on Wednesday as U.S. data hinted at inflationary pressure, although healthier enquiries lifted 10 year paper into mildly positive territory, dealers said.
A rise of 0.1 percent in October durable goods orders in the U.S. prompted market weakness. The average forecast was of a 2.0 percent fall.
Dutch bonds of almost all maturities dipped by up to 0.05 at the close.
Ten year paper, however, bucked the negative trend, although it ended the day only 0.01 higher.
In a thin day's business, Jan 2006 paper stood out with 585 million guilders worth changing hands.
The healthier buying also explained a modest widening of the spread under bunds from -6 basis points to -7 at ten years.
At the long end, the spread was unchanged at -19 bp, having opened at -21 bp.
Traders said there were signs that spreads under bunds were stabilising after pressure early in the week.
"Overall, the bidding is not too bad, so it doesn't look like the spreads will be changing too much," one trader said.
